prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1464; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss came in from the policyholder describing a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. Statements from two independent witnesses and the other driver describe the collision the same way the policyholder did, and scene photos line up with that account.

Entry 3: Vehicle inspection shows damage concentrated along the passenger side, which is consistent with the reported impact. No prior damage to the vehicle appears in our records or in the photos, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 4: The driver resides with the policyholder and qualifies as a covered household member under the policy. Coverage is confirmed for this loss, subject to the usual reservation for the remaining liability questions.

Entry 5: Medical records from the claimant's provider document a concussion. The diagnosed injury fits the type and force of the collision, and no earlier injury to the same body area is on file. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered as symptoms improved.

Entry 6: Through counsel, the claimant's account of the accident has stayed consistent across every conversation with our office. File is being prepared for liability and damages evaluation, with the attorney's demand expected next.
